item.title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
item.description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

item.title: Georgia has top College Football Playoff seed in sight with dominating road win over No 21 South Carolina
item.description: The Georgia Bulldogs suffocated South Carolina's offense at Williams-Brice Stadium as Nate Frazier scored two touchdowns in the top-ranked team's win.
item.content:encoded:
Georgia showed exactly why it is the top-ranked team in college football on Saturday.

The Bulldogs beat No. 21 South Carolina 34-6 at Williams-Brice Stadium, as the Georgia defense suffocated the Gamecocks' offense. With the win, Georgia now has the top spot in the College Football Playoff firmly in their grasp.

South Carolina had just 218 yards of offense on the day. South Carolina star quarterback LaNorris Sellers was held in check, as he completed just 10 of 18 passes for 87 yards and a touchdown.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

While South Carolina's offense never quite got out of the gate, it took Georgia a little bit of time to get things rolling.

The Gamecocks opened the game with a field goal, and the Bulldogs responded with a first-quarter field goal of their own, tying the game 3-3. South Carolina also converted a field goal on their second drive, going up 6-3.

The Bulldogs' offense didn't find the end zone until later in the second quarter, when it capped off a 10-play, 88-yard drive with a Nate Frazier touchdown, giving Georgia a 10-6 lead going into halftime.

Georgia got the ball to begin the third quarter, and they broke through with an explosive play. On third-and-2, quarterback Gunner Stockton found tight end Jaden Reddell for a 66-yard completion that brought Georgia to South Carolina's 1-yard line.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

A couple of plays later, Frazier punched the ball into the end zone for his second touchdown of the game, putting Georgia up 17-6. Later in the third quarter, the Bulldogs tacked on another field goal to go up 20-6.

The Bulldogs effectively put the game away when they marched down the field with an 11-play, 91-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. Wide receiver Craig Dandridge scored a 14-yard touchdown on a play fake that had South Carolina's defense fooled, putting Georgia up 27-6.

Georgia tacked on another touchdown at the end of the fourth quarter to go up 34-6, as they scored 31 unanswered points after falling behind 6-3.

Frazier had 23 carries for 94 yards and two touchdowns on the day for Georgia.

Georgia plays rival Georgia Tech in their next game on Saturday, and a win would all but guarantee the top seed in the College Football Playoff.

item.title: Three killed, one injured in shooting at Ohio baby shower, police say
item.description: Three people, including the unborn child's father, were killed at a baby shower shooting at Pandora's Magical Events Venue in Parma, Ohio, police say.
item.content:encoded:
Three people were killed and another was injured during a shooting at a baby shower at an Ohio event venue Saturday evening, according to local reports.

The shooting occurred around 6 p.m. inside Pandora's Magical Events Venue, located at 5331 Ridge Road in Parma, Ohio, according to a statement released by the Parma Police Department.

Responding officers determined that four people had been shot during an "exchange of gunfire."

A 17-year-old girl, a 19-year-old man and a 45-year-old man were found dead at the scene, according to police.

PREGNANT MOM JUST 4 DAYS FROM GIVING BIRTH AMONG 8 KILLED IN PENNSYLVANIA MASSACRE: REPORTS

Parma police Public Information Officer Scott Traxler told FOX 8/WJW that the 19-year-old victim was the unborn child's father and the 45-year-old victim was the pregnant woman's father. Police identified the 19-year-old man as one of those involved in the exchange of gunfire.

A fourth victim, a 39-year-old woman, suffered a gunshot wound to the leg that was considered non-life-threatening, police said.

Police also said a 29-year-old man allegedly involved in the exchange of gunfire was taken into custody following the shooting. Authorities have not publicly identified the man in custody or announced a possible motive.

Traxler told Fox News Digital that authorities were continuing to verify additional details surrounding the shooting.

Multiple firearms were recovered from the scene, according to police.

In a social media post, the Parma Police Department said officers were investigating a shooting involving multiple victims in the 5300 block of Ridge Road.

"Parma Police Department extends its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in this tragic incident," the department wrote.

"There is no danger to the public," police added.

Police said the families of those killed have been notified.

The Parma Police Department's Detective Bureau is investigating the shooting.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

item.title: Florida escapes against Vanderbilt courtesy of lucky bounce in another close SEC finish
item.description: Aaron Philo piled up 314 total yards and two touchdowns as Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators rallied late to edge Vanderbilt in a wild SEC finish.
item.content:encoded:
Florida’s 2026 season has been defined by highs and lows, and Week 12 delivered one of the Gators’ high points.

It took a late rally and a fortunate bounce, but in the end, Florida celebrated a 34-27 victory in front of more than 88,000 fans at The Swamp.

Florida quarterback Aaron Philo accounted for 314 yards and two touchdowns, while running back Jadan Baugh scored with just over two minutes left on the clock to complete the latest chapter in the Gators' up-and-down year.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I’ll take all the luck we can get," Florida head coach Jon Sumrall said. "We need it right now. We need all of it. I’m never going to be above taking luck."

Gators wide receiver Eric Singleton Jr. chipped in a career-high 117 yards receiving and had the play of the game.

Philo threw high to Micah Mays on third-and-5 in the fourth quarter, but the ball ricocheted into Singleton’s hands for a 37-yard gain. A roughing-the-passer penalty set Baugh up for his 16th touchdown of the season, a 10-yard scamper from the wildcat formation.

FLORIDA GATORS MAY OR MAY NOT BE ‘BACK,’ BUT ONE THING IS CERTAIN, FOOTBALL IS FINALLY FUN IN THE SWAMP AGAIN

"I didn’t know it was tipped," Philo, who was on the ground as the play unfolded, said. "I really didn’t know it was happening. But I’m glad it happened."

Vanderbilt has now dropped seven of their past eight games and will miss a bowl game for the first time since 2023. "We left too many plays on the field to beat a team that found a way in the critical moments to move the ball and score and to generate stops," Vandy coach Clark Lea said.

Commodores quarterback Jared Curtis threw two touchdown passes in the second quarter, including a 75-yarder to Junior Sherrill, to put Vanderbilt ahead 24-17 at halftime and draw a chorus of boos from the home team.

Saturday’s win marked the first time since late September that Florida had won consecutive games. The Gators also finished SEC play with a winning record for the first time since 2020.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Lane Kiffin takes the side exit as Tennessee sends LSU home and moves to the doorstep of CFP
item.description: Tennessee football fans threw golf balls onto the Neyland Stadium field as Lane Kiffin and LSU exited early, with the Vols now one win from the CFP.
item.content:encoded:
KNOXVILLE, Tenn. — Lane Kiffin took the side exit. Tennessee took another step toward the College Football Playoff on Saturday night.

On a night when golf balls again landed on the field at Neyland Stadium, the Volunteers beat LSU 27-13 to move within one win of a likely postseason berth.

The closing minutes turned ugly as students threw items onto the playing surface, prompting LSU players to move toward midfield while police worked to restore order.

CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE 'EXPLAINS' ITS LACK OF TRANSPARENCY: ISN'T REALLY 'FEASIBLE' | IAN MILLER

Kiffin and the Tigers eventually left through a side exit, heading home with their fifth loss of a season that began with championship expectations.

Tennessee, meanwhile, had plenty to celebrate.

On the same day Indiana and UCLA lost on the road, the Vols strengthened their playoff case with a defense that forced three turnovers, held LSU to 265 total yards and fed off a crowd that helped cause seven false-start penalties.

The 27-13 win over LSU should garner the Vols a number of points from the members that sit inside a gigantic room in Grapevine, Texas, looking at the "metrics."

Should that performance push Tennessee ahead of an Alabama team that played an FCS opponent Saturday? There’s certainly an argument for it, especially since the Vols already beat the Crimson Tide in Knoxville.

Will it? Given the committee’s affection for Alabama, don’t count on it.

For Josh Heupel, the more useful calculation is simple: Beat Vanderbilt next week, and Tennessee will be packing for the playoff, after securing a must-win against an LSU team overloading with expensive talent.

It was also in the same venue that hosted Lane Kiffin's return to Knoxville, which was met with a plethora of f-bombs dropped throughout the game.

Who would of thought at the beginning of this season, with LSU marching into the year as one of the most talked about teams in all of college football, that the Tigers would be suffering their fifth loss of 2026.

The former Vols coach heard plenty from a Neyland Stadium crowd that hasn’t forgotten his one season in Knoxville.

The expletives were predictable. So was the attention surrounding his return, even if he has stood on the visiting sideline here before.

But the football story belonged to Tennessee.

The Vols leaned on the formula that has carried them through the season: DeSean Bishop and the running game, a defense capable of taking over, and enough timely plays to finish the job.

It hasn’t always been pretty. It has been effective.

13TH-RANKED TENNESSEE DISMANTLES SIXTH-RANKED KENTUCKY TO STAY ALIVE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RACE

Even though Lane Kiffin was making his return to Knoxville, which has happened more times than you think, he was back on the sidelines coaching a different team inside a stadium he roamed the sidelines on.

The problem for the LSU head coach was that this story was not about him, at least this time.

No matter what took place over the last five minutes of this game, the story is about Tennessee being one-game closer to reserving its spot in the CFP.

Heck, you could make the argument that the Vols could afford another loss after the wild day that saw both Indiana and UCLA lose.

But, it doesn’t help that their final game of the regular season will come against Vanderbilt, which doesn’t help much with strength of schedule.

That's why, as Tennessee fans celebrated in the stands with "Dixieland Delight" following the win, you knew how important this game was for the program.

CFP HANGOVER: INDIANA CAN’T ESCAPE SCHEDULE DEBATE, BUT ALABAMA GETS TO SKIP THE CONVERSATION ONCE AGAIN

Was it the most critical game in the past decade? That's up for debate, even though there hasn’t been a game with these type of CFP implications in Knoxville.

"It's a different style that maybe I've played. Maybe the old times folks would appreciate the style of play. We've played field position more than I have before, but winning in all three phases of the game," Josh Heupel said postgame about the CFP committee.

Whether it's Faizon Brandon or George MacIntyre, the Vols found a way to use both quarterbacks against an LSU team known for its pressure on defense.

Was it perfect? Nope.

But, the Vols did rush for over 200 yards against an LSU team that has shined in that department throughout the season.

You might not like the way this football team is winning games. That's fine, by the way. But, you cannot deny that they are finding different ways to win these types of games. Also, they have done it with the weight of the world bearing down on them.

Nothing about this game from an offensive standpoint will be etched in the history books, and nor should it.

But, against a team that has $43 million worth of talent on its roster, it was Tennessee's inept offense that put together two touchdowns and a defense with crucial stops in the fourth quarter that led to them being one win away from the postseason.

You can say Tennessee doesn’t deserve to be ahead of Alabama, given that argument doesn’t seem to be going anywhere anytime soon.

But, you can't tell me they aren’t in the same "pod" any longer after the win over LSU. Both teams defeated Lane Kiffin, and it was Tennessee beating Alabama this season in Knoxville.

Maybe it doesn’t matter any longer, given the results that took place within the Big Ten on Saturday.

But at the expense of Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers, it's Tennessee that found another gear in the fourth quarter that sent the former Vols coach back to Baton Rouge to deal with an upset fan base.

As for Josh Heupel and the Vols, a trip to Nashville next week after Thanksgiving should turn into a CFP welcoming party.

item.title: Florida man sentenced to death for 'cold, calculated' murder of attorney whose body was never found
item.description: Former Florida plastic surgeon Tomasz Kosowski got the death penalty for murdering lawyer Cozzi, whose remains were never recovered after the 2023 killing.
item.content:encoded:
A former Florida plastic surgeon acting as his own attorney was sentenced to death Friday for the 2023 murder of an opposing lawyer whose remains were never recovered, court records show.

Pinellas County Judge Joseph Bulone imposed the death penalty on Tomasz Kosowski, 47, after denying a last-minute motion by Kosowski to disqualify the judge from the case, according to the Pinellas County court docket.

"The court has given great weight to the aggravating factor that the homicide was committed in a cold, calculated and premeditated manner, without any pretense of moral or legal justification," Bulone said in court, FOX 13 Tampa Bay reported, ruling that the nature of the killing alone outweighed all mitigating factors.

FLORIDA PUTS 77-YEAR-OLD MAN TO DEATH FOR DEPUTY'S MURDER AS STATE CLOSES IN ON EXECUTION RECORD

Bulone had found Kosowski guilty of first-degree murder in September following a non-jury trial, court records show.

The two men crossed paths through a civil lawsuit dating back to 2019, over medical billing money Kosowski claimed he was owed. Cozzi represented corporate clients Kosowski had sued, and prosecutors said Kosowski grew increasingly hostile toward the attorney during years of litigation.

Cozzi disappeared on March 21, 2023, minutes before a scheduled 10 a.m. teleconference hearing in the case, leaving his phone, keys and wallet on his desk at the Blanchard Law Firm in Largo, court records show.

Prosecutors said Kosowski killed Cozzi inside the firm's bathroom — where spattered blood mixed with Kosowski's DNA was found — and wheeled Cozzi's remains out in a heavy wagon covered with a reddish-orange blanket to a silver Toyota Tundra.

UNLICENSED MIAMI SURGEON 'DR. FRANKENSTEIN' VANISHES DAYS BEFORE TRIAL OVER BOTCHED PROCEDURES: AUTHORITIES

Surveillance cameras tracked the truck to Kosowski's Tarpon Springs home, where investigators executing a search warrant found Cozzi's DNA in the truck bed and on the garage floor, along with a vial of the paralytic drug succinylcholine tied to Kosowski's Miami plastic surgery practice, court records show.

Cellphone records placed Kosowski near a dumpster in Collier County near the Everglades, and investigators searched the landfill where its contents were taken after more than 6,000 tons of garbage had been piled onto the load, prosecutors said.

Cozzi's remains were never found, and the Public Defender's Office was appointed to represent Kosowski in his appeal, according to court records.

item.title: 17 major federal agencies flagged over cybersecurity gaps as watchdog warns of increased attack risk
item.description: A new Government Accountability Office report found 17 of 22 federal agencies, including HHS and DHS, failed to fully address zero trust guidance, raising cyberattack risks.
item.content:encoded:
A sweeping federal watchdog report found that 17 of 22 major civilian agencies failed to fully address key cybersecurity planning guidance, warning that the shortcomings could leave government systems more vulnerable to cyberattacks and operational disruptions.

The Government Accountability Office (GAO) released its findings this week, identifying gaps at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of State, Department of the Treasury and Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), among others.

The report examined whether agencies had incorporated selected federal guidance into their plans for implementing zero trust architecture, a cybersecurity approach requiring users, devices and systems to be verified before accessing protected networks.

RETIRED FBI AGENT WARNS NCIC BREACH COULD THREATEN POLICE SAFETY DURING TRAFFIC STOPS

Only five of the 22 agencies fully addressed the selected guidance as of August 2026, prompting GAO to issue 40 recommendations to the remaining 17.

"Agencies would therefore be at increased risk of cyberattacks that could interrupt operations or otherwise compromise agency resources," GAO warned.

HHS received six recommendations, the most of any agency reviewed, after investigators found that it lacked a documented enterprise-wide zero trust implementation plan covering all its information systems.

Although individual divisions were pursuing cybersecurity improvements, GAO warned that the absence of a unified strategy could prevent department leadership from maintaining a coherent view of its security modernization efforts.

HHS agreed with the recommendations and said it planned to develop an actionable department-wide strategy by the second quarter of fiscal year 2027.

CHINESE HACKERS TARGET NASA AND KEY US AGENCIES, DOJ ALLEGES

The Department of Commerce received four recommendations after investigators identified shortcomings in its cybersecurity planning documentation.

Commerce officials told GAO that staffing losses had significantly constrained the department's zero trust working group, limiting its ability to coordinate improvements and maintain comprehensive documentation.

At DHS, investigators found that the department had not fully documented cybersecurity maturity levels across all its high-value assets and high-impact systems. Officials attributed the incomplete assessments partly to lengthy government shutdowns during the preceding fiscal year.

DHS INVESTIGATES MASSIVE DATA BREACH EXPOSING 40,000 EMPLOYEES, INCLUDING ICE AND BORDER PATROL AGENTS

DOJ similarly cited resource constraints for incomplete assessments of critical systems, while State and Treasury were among the agencies that had only partially documented cybersecurity maturity levels.

GAO warned that incomplete assessments could leave agency leadership without the visibility necessary to determine where additional cybersecurity resources are needed.

Investigators also found that 11 agencies had only partially documented procedures for identifying actors within their IT environments, including certain non-person entities such as software applications and service accounts.

The watchdog warned that incomplete identification procedures could hinder efforts to ensure only authorized users and systems access government resources.

TRUMP’S NATIONAL CYBER DIRECTOR SEAN CAIRNCROSS FIRED AMID WIDESPREAD TECH OUTAGES

The findings come years after the Biden administration directed federal agencies to adopt zero trust cybersecurity principles through a 2021 executive order, followed by additional guidance in 2022 and 2024. Despite those directives, GAO found that 17 of 22 agencies still had not fully addressed selected cybersecurity planning requirements and guidance as of August 2026.

Thirteen agencies agreed with GAO's 40 recommendations, while four neither agreed nor disagreed. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission, one of the four, provided documentation demonstrating that it had already addressed both recommendations, which GAO verified.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and all 17 agencies identified in the report for comment.

"Absent a full implementation of ZTA requirements and guidance, agencies will lack an appropriate roadmap to fully incorporate and maintain an effective zero trust architecture," GAO concluded.

item.title: Raiders owner calls 'Madden' film an 'absolute crime' for its treatment of late father Al Davis
item.description: Mark Davis said he was "hurt" by the "Madden" movie's portrayal of his father Al Davis, blasting the Darryl Stingley scene as unfair to his dad's legacy.
item.content:encoded:
Al Davis became the Raiders’ head coach in 1963 and took over as the franchise's principal owner in 1972. In 1984, after the Raiders won their third Super Bowl, Davis coined the team’s famous motto: "Just win, baby."

Al Davis also had a stint as the Raiders general manager. He died in 2011. His son, Mark Davis, remains the team’s owner and oversees the franchise’s day-to-day operations. The Raiders relocated from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020.

Al Davis, a Pro Football Hall of Famer and central figure in NFL history, is portrayed in the newly released "Madden" film.

"Madden" chronicles the football career of the late John Madden, the legendary coach and broadcaster. The film’s casting and portrayals of real-life figures have sparked debate since its release on Prime Video earlier this week. Mark Davis joined the conversation, objecting to the way the movie depicted his late father.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I did the best I could to protect him. It's absolutely a crime that they're able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there's nobody around to protect their legacies. It's just unfair. I don't know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest," Davis told USA Today Sports about the on-screen depiction of his father.

Madden coached the Raiders for a decade, leading the franchise to its first Vince Lombardi Trophy.

Nicolas Cage plays the titular role in "Madden" while Academy Award winner Christian Bale co-stars as Al Davis.

The film’s more eccentric portrayals of sports figures were highlighted in an Associated Press review, which said the performances ran the "gamut from ‘SNL’-style parody to earnest drama."

Davis went on to describe "Madden" as a mashup of "Pulp Fiction," "Vacation" and "Saturday Night Live." That mix, however, was "not in a good way."

NFL FANS HORRIFIED BY NICOLAS CAGE'S JOHN MADDEN IMPRESSION IN UPCOMING MOVIE: 'EMBARRASSING'

Mark Davis said he did not fault the actors involved. "I don't blame Christian Bale. I don't blame Nicholas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do."

Mark Davis, who also owns the Las Vegas Aces, said the filmmakers contacted him to discuss certain aspects of the film.

One scene Davis said he preferred not to be included showed his father learning that New England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley had been injured during a 1978 preseason game between the Patriots and Raiders.

"For them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John [Madden] out of going to see him... that was just such a hurt to me personally because that's my father's legacy is how he treated people," Davis said.

"No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That's one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way."

The Raiders enter Week 11 at 4-6.

Las Vegas turned to rookie Fernando Mendoza last week after trading Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings at the trade deadline. Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in this year’s draft, threw for 143 yards in his first career NFL start, a 21-13 loss to the defending champion Seattle Seahawks.

item.title: NYC suspect in Chinatown fatal beating had 5 open cases as Mamdani pushes plan to close Rikers
item.description: Alexander Florentino faced five open cases before the fatal Chinatown attack, arriving as Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close Rikers Island by 2032.
item.content:encoded:
A 25-year-old homeless New York City man charged with beating a 62-year-old woman to death and assaulting a man in Manhattan's Chinatown was free despite five open criminal cases — including three arrests in November alone — just as Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close the city's Rikers Island jail.

NYPD officers arrested Alexander Florentino at 11:30 a.m. Saturday in the 5th Precinct on charges of murder, attempted murder, two counts of strangulation, burglary, assault and attempted assault.

New York State Unified Court System records show Florentino was awaiting Dec. 14 court appearances across five pending Manhattan Criminal Court dockets, meaning he had been released ahead of Friday's fatal attack.

ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF ATTEMPTED MURDER AT LARGE AFTER RIKERS RELEASE DESPITE ICE DETAINER: DHS

Most recently, police arrested Florentino on Nov. 18 in connection with an incident two days earlier, court records show. NYPD Transit Bureau officers also arrested him twice on Nov. 11 in separate cases tied to incidents on Nov. 11 and Aug. 3, and he had two open arrests from Sept. 2 and Sept. 28.

The repeat arrests came just a day after Mamdani unveiled a six-year plan to shutter Rikers Island by 2032 by cutting the jail population from roughly 6,700 to 4,100 and expanding alternatives to detention.

"Too many New Yorkers have experienced our criminal legal system as a revolving door, where they cycle in and out of jail because there is too little energy expended towards helping them rebuild their lives," Mamdani said Friday. "We have a legal and moral obligation to close Rikers."

PENN STATION STABBING VICTIM SLAMS MAMDANI, DA BRAGG FOR SUSPECT BEING FREE ON STREETS

Police said officers responded to 27 Catherine St. around 3: 22 p.m. Friday and found the 62-year-old woman unconscious and unresponsive with trauma to her face and neck. Emergency medical workers transported her to NYC Health + Hospitals/Bellevue, where she was pronounced dead.

Officers also found a 66-year-old man with a laceration to the right side of his face after being struck over the head with a glass bottle, police said. He was taken to Bellevue in stable condition.

Authorities have not released the woman's identity pending family notification, and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner will determine her cause of death. Police have not disclosed a possible motive or said whether Florentino knew the victims.

The Manhattan District Attorney's Office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

All in all, there are 22 unique radio stations in the game, and each of them offers a different soundtrack to your wheeling and stealing as you traverse through Leonida.

Being a huge fan of the series and music in general, I thought it would be fun to rank my six favorite "GTA VI" radio stations.

This wasn’t easy, as there are a ton of great stations to choose from, and I even had to omit a few that I really liked (sorry, Back Country Radio).

With that said, let’s rank the best that "GTA VI" has to offer in the form of music.

By virtue of hitting the "quantity over quality" metrics, Flash FM sneaks its way onto the list at number six.

Don't get me wrong, there are heaps of awful songs on this station, but there are some gems in there too.

Echosmith, Foster The People, Gwen Stefani, and MGMT will have Millennials bobbing their heads as they commit vehicular homicide (in the game), and newcomers like Ella Langley and Addison Rae offer enough to be passable cruising songs when there's nothing else on.

Flash FM isn't the stalwart it was back in the '80s for "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City," but there is enough fun to be had here for this station to find its way into the rotation.

This one might be a bit of a nostalgia pick for me, but I don't care.

Having grown up and gone to high school in South Florida, a lot of the songs on this station were popular right around the time my life was centered around algebra tests and getting rejected by chicks, so playing a game where I can drive around a virtual representation of my hometown while blaring rap songs that were popular 15 years ago is an auto win.

If you're into 2000s and 2010s rap, you'll probably have your radio dial locked on Dirty South Classics, with heavy hitters like Lil Wayne, Outkast, Drake, Rick Ross and even Jay Z being well represented here.

There is no better feeling than cruising Miami Beach at night listening to "No Lie" by 2Chainz, and it's even cooler when that is also a core memory from your adolescence, minus the cocaine and dead hookers.

Now we are getting into rarified air, and Vice City FM begins a string of stations with way more good than bad on them.

For those of you who wanted the '80s vibes of "Vice City" to carry over to the new game, you're in luck.

MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS

Vice City FM is a carryover from the old Playstation 2 game, and the songs you'll find on here will have you thinking you hopped in a DeLorean and landed in 1986.

Genesis, Culture Club, Lionel Richie, Billy Idol, The Cars and so much more, you'll be pulling out the AquaNet and legwarmers before your first hour of gameplay.

The neon lights of South Florida mesh perfectly with the 80s vibes, and this station makes for a cool nighttime drive soundtrack.

For an added bonus, Weird Al Yankovic is one of the in-game DJs, which I thought was a nice touch.

Metal, metal and more metal. That's what you're going to find on The Chamber.

While I'm partial to the older stuff, this station has a great mix of classic and newer metal to bridge the generational gap for headbangers.

If you're a spiritual Boomer like me, you'll be happy to know acts like Iron Maiden, Judas Priest, Megadeth and, of course, Metallica are littered all over The Chamber.

New-school metal disciples will be pleased to hear the likes of Linkin Park, System of a Down, Tool and Sepultura mixed in.

Committing virtual crimes is so much more fun when it's set to the brutal riffing and blistering solos of Judas Priest's "Freewheel Burning," but don't just take my word for it, try it yourself.

And hey, the station is hosted by Slayer's Tom Araya and Kerry King, so you know it's curated by two legends.

Can you name a better combination than the sun-soaked streets of South Florida and some soothing yacht rock?

Of course you can't, which is why Emotion 98.3 is sitting in the silver medal spot for "GTA VI" radio stations.

Emotion makes its triumphant return as one of the stations featured in "GTA: Vice City," and its setlist will have you looking for the nearest super yacht to steal so that you can enjoy the songs properly.

You want soft rock? How does Ace, Chicago, The Doobie Brothers, and Bruce Hornsby sound?

And that's just the tip of the iceberg.

I spent my entire life being serenaded by these guys while navigating the intracoastal waterways of South Florida, and now I get to do it in a video game.

Life sure is sweet sometimes!

It was never going to be anything else.

If you played "GTA: Vice City," you know how legendary this station was.

Well, it's back and better than ever, featuring a wide range of classic rock artists that offer the best company on any long drive around Leonida.

There are too many bangers to even count, but I'll try: Def Leppard, AC/DC, Aerosmith, Dire Straits, Foreigner, Blue Oyster Cult, Motley Crue, Styx, and ZZ Top, just to name a few.

Seriously, I haven't even mentioned another half dozen artists who rank as some of my favorites of all time.

Oh, and they have Van Halen, too. In case I needed to nerd out any more than I already am.

I also love how they included several Tom Petty songs, given his connection to the Sunshine State.

Finally, the station is hosted by Lindsey Buckingham of Fleetwood Mac fame and Michael Freaking McDonald.

When the king of Blue Eyed Soul is spinning tunes, it's probably a station worth listening to.

item.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix betting guide: How to bet Saturday night's race on the strip
item.description: Las Vegas Grand Prix betting picks: Kimi Antonelli to win at +470, Lando Norris podium, Charles Leclerc podium at +350 and Oscar Piastri as biggest mover.
item.content:encoded:
Vegas doesn't do anything quietly, and the Las Vegas Grand Prix is no exception. The lights are on, the casinos are packed and Formula One cars will be screaming down the Strip at more than 200 miles per hour Saturday night. It's the one race on the calendar that feels like a show as much as a sporting event.

The betting board fits the setting. You can lay heavy juice on the favorite, or you can do what Vegas is built for and take a few swings. The race also has one more ingredient that makes it great to bet: chaos. Las Vegas averages 48.7 overtakes per race, more than Monza, Baku or Jeddah. The starting grid is a suggestion here, not a guarantee.

Here's how to bet the Las Vegas Grand Prix, from the race winner to a couple of fun swings further down the board.

WHAT IS A PARLAY BET? — HOW PARLAYS WORK, PAYOUTS AND RULES EXPLAINED

Antonelli was the fastest driver in qualifying, 0.258 seconds clear of Verstappen. A five-place penalty for an extra engine component dropped him to sixth. Oscar Piastri, Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll took 10-place penalties, and Piastri starts 17th after qualifying seventh.

Odds via FanDuel

This is the bet. The fastest car on the track is starting sixth, and you're getting almost 5-1 on it.

Antonelli has already won this year's drivers' championship, and he's chasing his 10th win of the season. He out-qualified everyone by a quarter of a second, and Mercedes brought a turbocharger upgrade this weekend that only he is running. Russell is on the older spec.

Starting from behind hasn't slowed him down this year. He won at Monza from 19th on the grid and finished fifth in Baku from 16th. Both are high-speed, low-downforce tracks, just like Vegas. Throw in a circuit that produces almost 50 overtakes per race, and five spots isn't much to make up.

Norris is the steady play. He starts third, he has four straight top-five finishes, and he took pole here last year before finishing second, a result later wiped out by a post-race disqualification.

He's also been quick all weekend. Norris set the fastest second sector in qualifying and finished just 0.093 seconds behind Verstappen's lap. In Brazil, he beat Verstappen to the line by 14.6 seconds. Starting on the second row of a track where passing is easy, a top-three finish is a reasonable ask.

NFL BETTING STRATEGY GUIDE: HOW TO BET ON FOOTBALL

This is the Vegas swing.

Ferrari had a rough qualifying session, with both cars knocked out in Q2. After the penalties, Leclerc starts 10th. That's exactly why the price is +350, and exactly why I'm interested.

Leclerc has finished in the top four in all three of his Las Vegas starts. He's led 13 laps here, the third-most of anyone since the race began. He has six podiums this season, finished second at the U.S. Grand Prix and has finished in the top five in seven of his last eight races in North America.

Some drivers just have a feel for a track. Leclerc has one for this one. At 7-2, it's worth a bet.

Here's a fun one. Piastri qualified seventh, then a 10-place engine penalty dropped him to 17th on the grid.

The pace is there. He was within about a second of pole in qualifying, and he's running the same McLaren that Norris has on the second row. A fast car starting 17th on the highest-overtaking track of the season is a natural fit for this market. If he finishes anywhere in the top 10, he'll likely be among the biggest movers on the night.

Verstappen has won here twice, in 2023 and 2025, and he starts on pole. I understand why he's the favorite.

But -130 means risking $130 to win $100 on a single race, at a track where the polesitter has less protection than almost anywhere else, with the fastest car in the field coming up behind him. Under the Vegas lights, I'd rather bet on chaos than lay juice on the chalk.

item.title: Trump says Roger Clemens should be in the Baseball Hall of Fame 'immediately,' won't fully back Barry Bonds
item.description: Fresh off pardoning Pete Rose, President Donald Trump said Roger Clemens belongs in the Baseball Hall of Fame immediately, citing his seven Cy Youngs.
item.content:encoded:
After giving a "complete and total pardon" to Pete Rose, President Donald Trump now has his eyes on getting another baseball legend into Cooperstown.

Trump said that seven-time Cy Young Award winner Roger Clemens should be in the Baseball Hall of Fame "immediately." Trump noted that Clemens has never been proven to have taken performance-enhancing drugs.

"Roger Clemens has never been proven to have taken drugs, and he swears that he didn't. And he went through committees and everything else, and they — he actually won a court case. And Roger Clemens said and stated strongly he never took drugs," Trump said during an appearance on Fox News' "Saturday in America."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Trump was referencing the court case in June 2012, in which Clemens was acquitted of all six counts of perjury, making false statements and obstructing Congress after a retrial over his denials of using steroids. Trump gushed over Clemens' illustrious resume.

Nicknamed "Rocket" for his overpowering fastball, Clemens won seven Cy Youngs, the most in the history of the sport. He won the 1986 AL MVP, was an 11-time All-Star and a two-time World Series champion, and won the ERA title seven times.

While Trump was steadfast in his belief that Clemens belongs in the Baseball Hall of Fame, he did not offer the same endorsement for Barry Bonds.

"Barry Bonds, I think (denied taking drugs) too. But a lot of, I mean, look, he was such a great player, you know, he was a great player before the so-called drug excursion, if that ever took place," Trump said.

TRUMP SAYS HE'LL GIVE ROGER CLEMENS THE PRESIDENTIAL MEDAL OF FREEDOM: 'THIS SUPERSEDES ANYTHING I'VE DONE'

Bonds has never admitted to knowingly taking performance-enhancing drugs. The San Francisco Giants legend testified before a federal grand jury in 2003 that he unknowingly used a substance called "the clear," which is a designer anabolic steroid.

"The problem is he just looked like he took drugs," Trump said with a laugh.

"With Barry, it’s a little bit different (than Clemens) because there was very strong testimony and everything else," Trump said. "But I would consider. His numbers are so big, he was a great player and then he became a beyond great player."

Bonds' 762 home runs, 2,558 walks, 688 intentional walks and 162.8 bWAR are all MLB records. He was a seven-time MVP and a 14-time All-Star.

Bonds received 66% of the vote in his final year on the ballot, short of the 75% required to earn induction.

Clemens peaked at 65.2% in his final year on the ballot. Unfortunately for him, he isn't eligible to be voted in again until 2031 because he received fewer than five votes from the 16-member Contemporary Baseball Era Committee in Dec. 2025. As a result, he became ineligible for the next three-year cycle under Hall of Fame rules. Bonds, who also received fewer than five votes from the committee, isn't eligible until 2031, either.

item.title: Sammy Kershaw responds to 'sellout' critics after attending 2026 CMA Awards red carpet
item.description: Sammy Kershaw says talks with the Country Music Association went in a positive direction after he claimed he and wife Mendy were denied red carpet access.
item.content:encoded:
Sammy Kershaw is addressing critics directly who suspect that he "sold out" for attending the 2026 Country Music Association awards.

Speaking to Fox News Digital on the red carpet, the legendary country music singer explained how he spoke with the association after taking to social media to air out his grievances about the association allegedly denying him and his wife access to walk the red carpet.

"Well, it went great, and I'm not going to tell you all the details of what was said. All I can tell you is that I know things were going in a positive direction. So, when we decided that I was going to come to the show and walk the carpet, there's a few people out there that said things like, 'Oh, he sold out' and this and that. But that's not how I look at it," Kershaw began. 

ELLA LANGLEY DOMINATES CMA AWARDS WITH MAJOR WINS AS TAYLOR SWIFT MAKES STUNNING RETURN TO STAGE

"The way I look at it was, there was me and the CMA. And we came together and talked. We're moving in the right direction to a greater time in country music," Kershaw continued.

Without giving away details of the conversation, the country music star emphasized that both parties stayed for the whole conversation. "Nobody got up and walked away," he said.

Kershaw said that he didn't intend to hurt anyone with his Instagram post, but he was "heartbroken" by the association's decision.

"And then all of a sudden a lot of other people's fans came aboard. The fans, country music fans are country music fans, and they will bat for anybody in country music," Kershaw said. "Sometimes they'll get rough, but they came together for this because it was more than a carpet walk."

Kershaw claimed that he adjusted his tour schedule to accommodate this year's award show after being "strung along" for several months, assuming that they were invited.

"After more than 50 years in this business, many millions of records and singles streamed and sold, more than two dozen Billboard charted hits, a CMA Horizon Award nomination, being a lifetime CMA member, that they presented to me in 1992, and being asked to donate my time to play CMA Fest, I would hope I’ve earned the opportunity to walk the red carpet alongside my wife, as we’ve done before," Kershaw wrote.

He added, "I love country music, but never in a million years would I think that a successful country music entertainer (and I’m not the only one) would not be able to walk the red carpet. It’s extremely hurtful, embarrassing and very disappointing. I guess the next time I attend the CMA’s, it will be in tribute after I’m gone, if I’m lucky."

Country music stars poured into his comment section, supporting his message.

item.title: Retired FBI agent warns NCIC breach could threaten police safety during traffic stops
item.description: Retired FBI agent Jason Pack warns a hack of the National Crime Information Center could endanger officers at traffic stops if records were altered.
item.content:encoded:
A retired FBI supervisory special agent warned Saturday that a cyber intrusion into the bureau's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) could endanger police officers during traffic stops if hackers altered records inside the database.

Jason Pack, a former FBI supervisory special agent who worked in cybercrime and public information, told Fox News Digital that the bureau's incident response team must quickly determine whether data was manipulated inside the system, which feeds criminal records to patrol cars nationwide.

"What they worry about is if any of this data has changed, then it might affect officers' safety on the side of the road," Pack said, noting there is no indication yet that any records were altered or that the system is experiencing an outage.

FBI PROBES SECOND CYBERATTACK IN MONTHS AS HACKERS BREACH KEY CRIME DATABASE, SOURCES SAY

Three sources familiar with the matter told Fox News that hackers breached the NCIC, marking the second cyberattack against the bureau in months. The FBI is investigating how the intruders gained entry and whether any information was compromised.

In an interview with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany on Saturday morning, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the intrusion, adding, "I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that."

Pack described the NCIC as "America's computer for law enforcement," explaining that roughly 56 state terminals feed data out to hundreds of thousands of patrol car computers, so officers can check warrants, criminal histories, missing children, gang members and suspected terrorists.

FBI SAYS SOURCE OF ITS JOBS PORTAL BREACH STILL UNKNOWN AS HACKERS ALLEGE EMPLOYEE DATA COMPROMISED

While the database does not hold classified intelligence or sensitive FBI investigative case files, Pack said it stores personally identifiable information, including names, dates of birth and Social Security numbers.

Investigators will examine IP logs and metadata to determine whether attackers exploited a compromised password among the system's more than 100,000 users, breached a state terminal or infiltrated through a third-party vendor, Pack said, adding that cyberattacks have accelerated to "machine speed" as criminals increasingly use artificial intelligence to probe for vulnerabilities.

"You have this cat and mouse game where cybersecurity experts are trying to patch the vulnerabilities that they find. They're looking for their own vulnerabilities at the same time, they have to play defense against the criminals who are out there trying to steal information or do harm to our systems. I think we're just seeing now this speed of these intrusions ramp up a lot," Pack said.

TECH OUTAGE CASCADE EXPOSES US VULNERABILITIES TO FOREIGN CYBER THREATS

The intrusion follows a September cyberattack in which the extortion group ShinyHunters breached an FBI job portal website and claimed to steal personal records belonging to bureau employees.

The latest incident also comes as a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report found 17 of 22 government agencies were not in compliance with federal cybersecurity regulations.

The FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the NCIC breach.

Fox News Digital's James Cirrone and Greg Norman-Diamond, and Fox News' David Spunt contributed to this report.

item.title: Utah vs TCU prediction, odds and best bets: Utah faces a big time trap spot
item.description: Utah vs. TCU betting preview: Why TCU +7.5, the Horned Frogs moneyline and the under 46.5 are the plays for Saturday night in Fort Worth.
item.content:encoded:
Utah has done everything right this season. The Utes are 10-0, No. 2 in the College Football Playoff rankings and riding a 16-game winning streak dating to last season. They're in line for a first-round bye, and in Morgan Scalley's first year, they're the best story in the Big 12.

That's also why Saturday night in Fort Worth is a dangerous spot for the Utes.

Over the last two weeks, Utah has played two games that would drain any team. It beat rival BYU 28-20 in the Holy War, then had to rally for a 40-39 win at Arizona which was a bit of a letdown spot in its own right. Now the Utes are on the road again, for a 9:00 p.m. ET kickoff against a TCU team fighting for bowl eligibility, with one of the best defenses in the country, in what will surely be a rowdy atmosphere.

FIVE COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETS FOR SATURDAY, INCLUDING TWO ROAD DOGS THAT ARE BEING SLEPT ON

The market sees an unbeaten team against a .500 team. I see a letdown spot, a defense built to slow Utah down and a lot of bad luck about to turn around.

Utah -265 | TCU +215
Spread: Utah -7.5 (-105) | TCU +7.5 (-115)
Total: 46.5 (Over -110 / Under -110)

Saturday, Nov. 21, 9 p.m. ET, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth, FOX

This is about as lopsided as a betting market gets. Between 82% and 90% of the spread tickets are on Utah, and the Utes have drawn between 73% and 84% of the money.

The line has moved around with that action. Utah opened at -6.5, climbed as high as -7.5 and has settled between -7 and -7.5 depending on the book. The public is backing the undefeated team with the shiny ranking, and the books are happy to take it.

I love a classic contrarian spot, and in this one, I'm happy to go the other way.

WHAT IS A TEASER BET? HOW TEASERS WORK IN FOOTBALL AND BASKETBALL BETTING

Spots like this are where unbeaten teams lose.

Utah has been in close games almost every week since late September, and the last two were especially challenging. Winning a rivalry game against BYU and then rallying on the road at Arizona takes a lot out of a roster. This is the third straight week the Utes have played a meaningful, high-stress game, and it's another road trip with a late kickoff.

Don't get me wrong, I fully understand that Utah's offense is still dangerous. Devon Dampier has accounted for 31 touchdowns, 22 passing and nine rushing, and the Utes are scoring 37.9 points per game, 15th in the country. But this is the kind of game where good teams can look flat for a half, and against this defense, a flat half can be enough to put the Utes in trouble.

ESPN DISMISSES UTAH UTES AS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP CONTENDERS DESPITE BIG WIN OVER BYU: 'THEY WON'T WIN'

Utah's offense isn't the only elite unit in this one. TCU's record hides how good its defense has been. The Horned Frogs allow just 15.2 points per game, 12th in the country, and they rank ninth nationally in net adjusted EPA per play allowed.

That's the matchup that matters. TCU has been at its best against offenses like Utah's. Under Sonny Dykes, the Horned Frogs are 17-7 straight up and 15-8-1 against the spread against teams averaging at least 425 yards per game. Dykes is also 6-3 against the spread as an underdog of 3.5 to 10 points, right in the range of this line.

This is the stat that makes the case, and I promise it's not a stretch. TCU has lost five games this season, and all five were decided by one score. Against Power 4 opponents, the Horned Frogs are 1-5 in one-score games, the most such losses of any Power 4 team. They've battled, but things have consistently gone against the Horned Frogs in close ones.

On the other side, Utah is 4-0 in those games. One could make the argument that good teams find a way to win those games, and that's true. But it's also true that there is some inherent luck in close games, and expecting that to always go your way i playing with fire.

Close-game records rarely hold over a full season. TCU hasn't been five losses worse than its opponents. It's been a handful of plays worse. Utah hasn't been four wins better, either. Eventually those coin flips start landing the other way, and a home game against a conference opponent with national championship aspirations is a good place for that to start for TCU.

WHAT IS A MONEYLINE BET? — HOW MONEYLINE ODDS, PAYOUTS AND FAVORITES WORK

It's only fair to make Utah's case too. The Utes are 8-2 against the spread and 7-1 as favorites of 6.5 or more. They score at an elite rate, and their defense allows only 18.6 points per game, 21st in the country.

TCU's offense is the real concern. The Horned Frogs score just 23.4 points per game, 103rd nationally, and they've been inconsistent all season. If Jaden Craig, who has thrown one interception over the last three games, can't move the ball, TCU's defense will eventually wear down.

That's why the points matter. I don't need TCU to outscore Utah. I need its defense to keep this within a score. If you're not a true believer in TCU at home, take the points.

This is the main play. Utah is in a letdown spot, the public is lopsided and TCU's defense is good enough to keep this close. The Horned Frogs have lost five games by a combined handful of plays. Getting more than a touchdown at home with that profile is the best number on the board.

If you believe in the letdown, take a smaller piece of the upset. At +215, the moneyline implies TCU wins about 32% of the time. With a top-12 scoring defense at home against a tired team on the road, that feels low.

The total fits the same story. TCU games have gone over just twice in 10 tries, and the Horned Frogs have averaged only 18.3 points per game in conference play. The early under action has been heavy, with every tracked ticket and dollar on the total backing the under.

If TCU's defense keeps Utah out of rhythm and its own offense grinds, this lands in the low 40s. That's the type of game where the underdog covers.

Utah is a great team, and it may still be a great futures bet to win the national title. But a 10-0 team playing its third straight high-stress game, on the road, late at night, against a top-12 defense with nothing to lose is how upsets happen.

Give me TCU +7.5 (-115), a sprinkle on the TCU moneyline (+215) and the under 46.5 (-110).
